ST-01.title: Fix nightly trailing-stop ratchet to apply breakeven floor for profitable positions

sign_off_record.findings: Confirmed via git blame that both live stop-writing entry points have called the floored calculate_trailing_stop() since commit b410cfa3c (2026-02-12), predating this cycle. position_manager.py confirmed off the live path. WDC worked example reproduced exactly. Non-blocking: fixed a misleading comment in test_trailing_stop_breakeven_floor.py's test_live_endpoints_call_calculate_trailing_stop (incorrectly implied a 3rd substring match came from the import statement).

ST-01.notes: Investigation (BLG-BE-102 scope item 1) confirmed both live production stop-writing paths (services/position_service.py::get_positions_with_prices() -> analyze_positions(), invoked nightly via GET /positions/analyze per .github/workflows/daily-snapshot.yml; and run_nightly_trailing_stop_update() via POST /positions/nightly-stop-update) already call the shared, floored calculate_trailing_stop() (backend/utils/calculations.py) -- trailing_stop = max(current_stop, new_stop, entry_price) when profitable. position_manager.py's own inline calc (max(current_stop, new_stop), no floor) is confirmed via code-path audit to be a backtest-tool-only path (only cross-module export used in production is check_market_regime, unrelated to stop calc) -- never imported by services/position_service.py or any live-serving endpoint. AC1 (single calc path in production) is therefore already satisfied by current code; documented via 2 new regression tests (TestPositionManagerNotOnLiveStopPath) confirming this structurally, not just narratively. AC3 (regression test, breakeven-floor case) added: tests/test_trailing_stop_breakeven_floor.py, 7 tests, using the exact BLG-BE-102 WDC worked example (508.80/54.1986/163.31/434.30 -> 434.30). AC2 (no open profitable position has current_stop below entry_price) is the sprint_backlog.md-flagged staging-only AC for this story -- requires a live-position DB query, not CI-reproducible; the item's own Notes field defers backfill/recompute of existing open positions to after this fix is verified, i.e. a post-merge ops action, not a code-commit deliverable. No production code change was needed for the floor logic itself (already correct); this story's real deliverable is the confirmation + regression test + explicit position_manager.py/live-path documentation closing the ambiguity BLG-BE-102 raised.

ST-02.title: Fix currency basis of current_trailing_stop/stop_price for US-market positions

sign_off_record.role: Backend Engineering Patterns Owner; Frontend Specifications & UX Documentation Owner
sign_off_record.findings: current_trailing_stop_native verified correctly computed and consumed across PositionCard.js, Positions.js table row, and TrailStopModal; trailBreached GBP-vs-GBP comparison confirmed unaffected. Pre-existing e2e fixture updates (epic01-v62-stops-alerts.spec.js, epic01-v70-grid-badge-parity.spec.js) confirmed to preserve original test intent (badge/label assertions only, no numeric stop assertion). DEV-EPIC01-ST02-01 filing and doc version bumps confirmed correctly formatted.

ST-02.notes: Root cause confirmed exactly as described in BLG-BE-103: get_positions_with_prices() (backend/services/position_service.py) returns initial_stop unconverted (native) but current_trailing_stop and stop_price GBP-converted for US-market positions, while PositionCard.js/Positions.js derive currencySymbol solely from position.market (native) and rendered current_trailing_stop next to it. Fix: added current_trailing_stop_native field to the backend response (native basis, mirrors the pre-existing stop_price_native pattern); frontend now renders current_trailing_stop_native on both Card and Table views, keeping the GBP-basis current_trailing_stop only for the (already GBP-consistent) breach comparison against current_price. Also corrected a related native-fallback bug in the TrailStopModal (Positions.js) that defaulted to the GBP stop_price instead of stop_price_native before its own live query resolves. Filed as DEV-EPIC01-ST02-01 in docs/specs/frontend/pages/positions.md#Known Deviations (spec already required 'native currency' display -- implementation diverged from v6.2 -- resolved same-story, so deviations_filed=true with the deviation documented as resolved, per the spec's DEV-EPIC01-ST05-01 precedent format). 2 pre-existing e2e fixtures (epic01-v62-stops-alerts.spec.js, epic01-v70-grid-badge-parity.spec.js) needed a 1-line makePosition() update each (default current_trailing_stop_native to mirror current_trailing_stop unless overridden) to keep testing their original scenarios under the corrected field -- both re-verified passing, confirmed via full re-run of both files (25/25 pass) plus a full 6-file trailing-stop-adjacent e2e sweep (57/57 pass) and the full backend suite (1170 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed). New coverage: tests/test_position_currency_basis.py (pytest, 2 tests) + tests/e2e/position-stop-currency-basis.spec.js (Playwright, 2 tests, V-CURR-01/V-CURR-02) -- both verified failing-then-passing against the actual fix (ran against pre-fix code first via the two pre-existing-fixture failures, confirming the tests are not trivially-passing).

ST-03.title: Add trailing_stop_action_rate spec entry with validation tolerances

sign_off_record.findings: Validation Tolerances subsection reviewed against the pre-existing Trailing Stop Action Rate definition — numeric bounds are internally consistent and satisfy the 'numerically, not qualitatively' AC.

ST-03.notes: The 'Trailing Stop Action Rate' section in metrics_definitions.md already existed (added v1.13.0 BLG-SPEC-61, extended v1.15.0 ST-07/BLG-BE-50) with Definition, Data Capture Requirement, and Tooling Assessment subsections -- BLG-SPEC-85's premise ('shipped without a formal entry') was stale by the time this story executed. The genuine gap against this story's AC ('tolerances stated numerically, not qualitatively') was the absence of an explicit numeric tolerance-band subsection. Added ## Validation Tolerances subsection: insufficient-sample threshold (denominator < 5), expected range (0.05-0.95 with denominator >= 5), anomalously low/high bands (< 0.05 / > 0.95 with denominator >= 10), stale-capture window (> 30 days with no new log row while eligible open positions exist), and the pre-existing 24h capture window restated for completeness. Doc version bumped 1.16.1 -> 1.17.0, Document History row to be appended at commit.

ST-13.title: Decide and apply treatment for trade_plans.setup_type with no default/required guarantee
ST-13.unblock_criteria: A decision recorded (required field / default value / accept-as-is with rationale); if a fix is chosen, implemented; Product Owner sign-off.

sign_off_record.findings: Decision: (b) -- normalize null/absent/empty setup_type to the existing canonical value "Other" server-side in create_plan()'s _create() closure. Rationale: "Other" already exists as the 6th canonical SETUP_TYPE_OPTIONS value in both backend and frontend dropdown, so defaulting to it costs nothing in new UI/enum/spec; applying server-side (not just frontend) covers direct API use too, which a required-field frontend change would not reach. Does not trigger a design-gate return per RISK-04 -- no new UI pattern, Other is already a live selectable option on this form.

ST-13.notes: Escalation ESC-EXEC-20260818-01 resolved same-session (well within the 24h SLA) -- decision made via agent-mediated Product Owner review, implemented, tested (4 new tests, tests/test_trade_plan_setup_type_default.py), documented (trade_plan_endpoints.md v0.12->v0.13).
